“For Rent” signs are replacing restaurant menus on Khreshchatyk. Russian attacks are emptying central Kyiv, while blackouts, water outages, soaring fuel costs, and staff shortages make serving the remaining customers harder, Reuters reports.

Even customers who come are cutting back. Borysova says the average order has fallen from three items to two. Curfews limit trading hours, and property damage adds another bill. Scores of hospitality businesses have closed or suspended operations, at least through winter.

Two of Borysova’s restaurants are scheduled to reopen in April, if the alarms allow.

Huang Returns, Nvidia Jumps 30%

Nvidia’s board brought back Jensen Huang, the CEO it had ousted over an extramarital affair with a Chinese spy. Nvidia stock rose about 30% at Monday’s open, and the S&P 500 added almost 5%. The shares have lost nearly half their value over the past six weeks, during the leadership turmoil.

The Nasdaq rose more than 6%. Sandisk, Intel, and Micron each gained about 15%. The S&P 500 had dropped 8.6% last week, its worst week since April 2025. That left it in a correction, more than 11% below its early-October peak.

The rally had a head start. The index was already expected to open higher before the Huang news added to the gain. The sell-off had other causes. Investors doubt that A.I. earnings can justify the spending, debt is getting more expensive for data-center builders, and tougher rules may be coming on chip exports to China and on new data centers. Traders also expect the Fed to raise rates by a quarter point next month. Nvidia’s own record-breaking earnings and Anthropic’s IPO did not stop last week’s slide.

On Monday, one executive’s return appeared to move the market more than a record earnings report had. A strategist at Jefferies says funds have not finished cutting their A.I. holdings. Inflation data arrives Wednesday, and the market is closed Thursday for Thanksgiving.
